newsitem.title: UK: Shell confirms $10 billion investment plan.
newsitem.headline: Shell confirms $10 billion investment plan.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group on Thursday said its U.S. subsidiary Shell Oil will invest up to $10 billion over the next four years on deep-water oil and gas projects in the Gulf of Mexico.
"It is an important, exciting and technologically challenging area to work," John Jennings, managing director of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, told reporters.
"The $10 billion should be seen in the context of the overall group's capital investment programme which is annually in the $10 to 12 billion range," he added.
Shell Oil already has two 1,000 metre deep-water projects in the Gulf of Mexico -- Mars and Auger -- and said in August it was preparing to plumb even greater depths.
The Financial Times earlier today reported from New Orleans that Shell Oil wants to start working on nine new projects in the Gulf of Mexico before 2001.
"It is a continuing development of deep-water fields in the Gulf of Mexico," said Jennings in reaction to the FT report.
He was speaking at a news conference on the official signing of a venture between Shell and Russia's Rosneft oil company to jointly take a 7.5 percent stake in the Caspian Pipeline Consortium.
Analysts said they would welcome Shell's planned investment in the Gulf of Mexico. "It is good news. They are investing where the money is," said analyst Jurjen Lunshof at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
Low development costs and a readily available infrastructure mean that the Gulf of Mexico is a profitable upstream area for Royal Dutch/Shell Group, said John Toalster at SocGen.
"It is very profitable oil," he said.
At 1413 gmt, Shell shares in London were up 10 pence at 983p.
